capabilities: Start a local MCP HTTP server exposing vault notes to Codex
Export active-note context and create request files for Codex
Import Codex replies by appending them or creating new notes
Summarize selected text or the active note into a daily note with an AI API
Expose MCP tools to search, read, write, append, and list notes
extras: Desktop-only; the MCP server binds to 127.0.0.1 and requires bearer-token authorization. AI summarization is optional and needs no key for the file bridge or MCP server. UI supports English and Chinese. Docs include a security section warning against sharing tokens or exposing the endpoint publicly.
problem: AI agents like Codex have no built-in way to search, read, and write vault notes without a hardcoded vault path or manual file handling.

relations.evidence: codex-bridge is a desktop-only plugin that connects your local vault to Codex.
For Codex-side usage, install the companion obsidian-connect skill.

summary: Local bridge that connects an Obsidian vault to Codex through file-based commands and a localhost MCP server for search, read, and write access.
